content.thinking:
I'm working out who was hit: the cause says the older version couldn't read the newer entry type, so shoppers whose spending summary was saved in that format and served by the old version saw their account page fail. Peak error rate isn't needed, just the duration and customer loss.

I'm noting that nobody was paged, so there was no cost to responders. The fix was a rollback by Argus, which has been confirmed and is still in place, with automatic sync left off. I'll avoid "brief" and won't say "likely," since the cause doesn't call it that.

input.overview: For {duration}, some shoppers on io-shop found that their account pages would not load, and at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests failed. A new version of the shop changed the way it saves each shopper's spending summary. The update got stuck part of the way through, so the older version was still running alongside the new one. The older version could not read summaries saved in the new way, so it failed the account pages of shoppers whose summaries had been saved that way. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. No on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged. Argus ended the problem by rolling the io-shop deployment back to the previous version. The rollback is confirmed and still in place, and automatic sync has been left off.
